'''Richard C. Powell''' (born 1939) is an American professor emeritus of physics and vice president emeritus of the [[University of Arizona]] (UA), whose career focused on research in materials science and laser optics. He served as president of the [[Optical Society of America]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.osa.org/aboutosa/leadership/pastpresidents/default.aspx|title=Past Presidents of the Optical Society of America|publisher=Optical Society of America|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090120044158/http://osa.org/aboutosa/leadership/pastpresidents/default.aspx|archivedate=January 20, 2009}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Powell was born in [[Lincoln, Nebraska]], and was reared in [[Ottumwa, Iowa]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.osa.org/osaorg/media/osa.history/Transcripts/Richard_Powell_InterviewRev.pdf|title=Interview with Richard Powell (Part 1 of 3)|last=Kinnane|first=Adrian|date=February 19, 2012|website=Optical Society of America|access-date=April 18, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170419101553/http://www.osa.org/osaorg/media/osa.history/Transcripts/Richard_Powell_InterviewRev.pdf|archive-date=April 19, 2017}}</ref> He graduated from the [[United States Naval Academy|U.S. Naval Academy]] in 1962, and took his commission in the [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] because the Air Force offered immediate support for study in a Ph.D. program.<ref name=":0" /> At [[Arizona State University]] he earned an M.S. and also completed a Ph.D. in physics there in 1967.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Powell completed his military service at the [[Air Force Cambridge Research Laboratories]] and then worked as a civilian at [[Sandia National Laboratories|Sandia National Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" /> He taught at [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Oklahoma State University–Stillwater|Oklahoma State University]] and the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico|Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico]], Instituto de Fisica.<ref name=":0" /> Powell joined the faculty of the [[University of Arizona]] as a professor of optical sciences and of materials science and director of the Optical Sciences Center. He later served as vice president for research and graduate studies, and upon retirement, became professor emeritus of optical sciences.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.photonics.com/Article.aspx?AID=21642|title=UA Optical Center Honors Innovators|date=April 4, 2005|website=Photonics media|access-date=2017-04-18}}</ref>

Following his retirement, he became a senior fellow at the UA Science and Tech Park, expanding "their Solar Zone to test, evaluate and demonstrate solar technologies."<ref name=":2" />

== Publications ==
Powell has written textbooks and published 260 research articles on laser spectroscopy and solid state laser development.<ref name="Drake2006">{{cite book|author=Gordon W. F. Drake|title=Springer Handbook of Atomic, Molecular, and Optical Physics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Jj-ad_2aNOAC&pg=PA1419|year=2006|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-0-387-26308-3|pages=1419–}}</ref>

His textbooks are ''Physics of Solid-State Laser Materials,'' <ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/us/book/9781563966583|title=Physics of Solid-State Laser Materials|last=Powell|first=Richard C.|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=1998|isbn=978-1-56396-658-3|location=New York|pages=|language=en|series=Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics Series|archive-date=2017-05-18|access-date=2017-09-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518141631/http://www.springer.com/us/book/9781563966583|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Symmetry, Group Theory, and the Physical Properties of Crystals,''<ref>{{Cite book|title=Symmetry, Group Theory, and the Physical Properties of Crystals|volume = 824|last=Powell|first=Richard C|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=2010|isbn=978-1-4419-7597-3|location=New York|pages=|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-1-4419-7598-0|series = Lecture Notes in Physics|url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/1338617}}</ref> and with Baldassare Di Bartolo, ''Crystal Symmetry, Lattice Vibrations and Optical Spectroscopy of Solids.''<ref>{{Cite book|title=Crystal Symmetry, Lattice Vibrations and Optical Spectroscopy of Solids|last=Di Bartolo|first=Baldassare|last2=Powell|first2=Richard C|publisher=World Scientific|year=2014|isbn=978-981-4579-20-9|location=|pages=|language=en-US|doi=10.1142/9052}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
The University of Arizona honored Powell as an innovator with a 2005 Technology Innovation Award for "moving UA technology out of the laboratory and into the marketplace."<ref name=":1" /> Powell is an elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], and also an elected Fellow of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.optics.arizona.edu/news-events/news/quicknews/reflections-richard-c-powell|title=Reflections: Richard C. Powell {{!}} College of Optical Sciences {{!}} The University of Arizona|last=Orr|first=Tammy|date=March 30, 2017|website=www.optics.arizona.edu|access-date=2017-04-18|archive-date=2018-11-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181102050025/http://www.optics.arizona.edu/news-events/news/quicknews/reflections-richard-c-powell|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 1999, he was also elected to the Russian Academy of Engineer Science.<ref name=":2" />
